get.description:
Pokémon in Pokédex order, one page at a time, optionally filtered by name, type and form,
and by whether PokéAPI still lists them.

To get the next page, pass the response's `next_cursor` as `cursor`, keeping the same
filters; it's `null` on the last page. Alternate forms, such as Mega Evolutions and regional
forms, are numbered from 10001, so they come after the main Pokédex.

post.description:
Starts a session: the response sets the session cookie, which later requests send back.

Sessions last 30 days, and using one in its last 15 renews it for another 30.

delete.description: Ends the session and clears its cookie. Signing out when signed out does nothing.

get.description:
The user's teams, most recently changed first, each with its Pokémon in slot order.
Teams with no Pokémon yet are listed too.

put.description:
Creates a team with the `id` you choose, a new UUID, and any Pokémon to start with.

Sending the same `id` again returns the team it made, unchanged, with 200 instead of 201, so
a create that's retried can't make two teams. An `id` someone else has is a 409, and a Pokémon
`id` that no Pokémon has is a 422.

parameters.name: team_id

schema.description: The team's `id`: a UUID its creator chose.
schema.title: Team Id

parameters.description: The team's `id`: a UUID its creator chose.

401.description: Sign in first: POST /api/session with your username and password sets the session cookie.

409.description: The change can't be made to the team as it is now: `detail` says why, and `reason` gives it as a code.

Puts a Pokémon in the team's next free slot. A team holds up to six, one of each species:
Charizard and Mega Charizard X can't share one. An `id` with no Pokémon is a 422.

Pokémon is on the team already, it moves into the slot and the gap it leaves closes. An `id`
with no Pokémon is a 422.

One way a species evolves from the one before it in the latest games: what sets it off,
and any conditions on top. Conditions that don't apply are `null` or `false`. Items, moves,
species and places are named as in PokéAPI, e.g. `thunder-stone`.
